sources.content:
A live intelligence dashboard tracking how Anthropic's AI releases impact public markets. Auto-detects new announcements, correlates with stock price drops, and identifies opportunity windows before the market prices them in.
Based on @brett_eth's methodology.
- Announcement Detection — Searches the web and Anthropic's newsroom for new model releases, capability updates, and product launches
- Sector Mapping — Maps each announcement to the public-market sectors it threatens (SaaS, Cybersecurity, Legal, Financial Analysis, IT Consulting, Healthcare, etc.)
- Stock Correlation — Pulls live stock prices for 26 tracked tickers via Yahoo Finance and checks for significant drops (>5% daily or >8% weekly)
- Signal Classification:
  - Confirmed Hit — Anthropic announcement + correlated stock drops already observed
  - Opportunity Window — Announcement maps to a sector, but stocks haven't moved yet (most actionable signal)

anthropic-hit-list/
├── index.html          # Frontend dashboard (single-file HTML/CSS/JS)
├── cgi-bin/
│   └── data.py         # API endpoint — serves stock data + hits as JSON
├── refresh.py          # Standalone stock price refresh script

- Two-column editorial layout: Confirmed Hits (red) | Projected Targets (blue)
- Live stock prices with daily/weekly/monthly change on hover
- Dynamically renders new hits detected by the intelligence engine
- Graceful fallback to static data if API is unavailable
- Responsive design, staggered load animations
- CGI script serving JSON to the frontend

- Yahoo Finance v8 batch spark API for stock data

- Reads each announcement to determine sector impact
- Correlates with live stock data
- Writes new hits to the dashboard database
- Sends push notifications for opportunity windows
- Fetches live prices for all 26 tickers from Yahoo Finance
- Calculates daily, weekly, and monthly percentage changes
- Updates the SQLite cache
- Outputs notable movers (>2% daily change)
- Stock Prices: Yahoo Finance v8 Spark API (no API key required)
- Announcements: Anthropic newsroom (anthropic.com/news), web search, tech press
- Methodology: Correlating AI capability announcements with public market impact
Analysis only. Not financial advice. This tool identifies patterns between AI announcements and stock price movements — it does not make trading recommendations.

sources.title: Anthropic Claude Model Release Timeline - Model Family Tree, Capability Evolution, and Platform Availability | hidekazu-konishi.com
sources.content:
Anthropic Claude Model Release Timeline - Model Family Tree, Capability Evolution, and Platform Availability
First Published: 
Last Updated: 
I summarize the model family tree of Claude Opus, Claude Sonnet, and Claude Haiku - now joined by the Mythos-class tier above Opus introduced with Claude Fable 5 - the full chronology of major releases with links to the official
anthropic.com/news/ announcements, the evolution of capabilities (context window, vision, tool use, computer use, prompt caching, extended thinking, memory tool, 1M context, effort parameter), the differences in availability across the Anthropic API, Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud (Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, formerly Vertex AI), and Microsoft Foundry, and the lifecycle of deprecated and retired Claude models as listed on Anthropic's official model deprecation page.
Companion articles on hidekazu-konishi.com:
- AWS History and Timeline regarding Amazon Bedrock - Overview, Functions, Features, Summary of Updates, and Introduction
- Amazon Bedrock Model Catalog 2026
- Claude Code Features and Settings Reference 2026
Overview - From Anthropic's Founding to Claude Opus 5.5
Anthropic was founded in 2021 as an AI safety company by former OpenAI researchers, and published the paper "Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI Feedback" in December 2022 introducing the training method that has since shaped every Claude model.
The first publicly available Claude model arrived on March 14, 2023, when Anthropic launched the Anthropic API with Claude and Claude Instant.
Three years later, as of the time of writing, the Claude family covers three named size tiers - Opus, Sonnet, and Haiku - introduced together with Claude 3 in March 2024, joined in June 2026 by the Mythos-class tier that sits above the Opus class, whose current generation is Claude Fable 5.1, announced on September 1, 2026.
Across these three years, Claude has been the first foundation model from a frontier lab to reach a 100K-token context window (May 2023), an early adopter of vision input across all model tiers (Claude 3, March 2024), the launch model for Computer Use as a public beta capability (Claude 3.5 Sonnet new, October 2024), and the introduction point for the extended-thinking and hybrid-reasoning paradigm in a production model (Claude 3.7 Sonnet, February 2025).
The 4.x generation that started in May 2025 brought a 1-million-token beta context window, the
effort parameter that lets developers trade off speed against capability, an explicit memory tool, and incremental coding gains that have made Claude Opus 4.x the default model for several AI-coding agent products. Claude Opus 4.8 (May 28, 2026) shifts the emphasis toward honesty and reliability - Anthropic reports it is roughly four times less likely than Opus 4.7 to let flaws in code it has written pass unremarked - and ships alongside a Dynamic Workflows research preview in Claude Code that orchestrates hundreds of parallel subagents.
Less than two weeks later, on June 9, 2026, Anthropic announced Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5, the first models in the new Mythos-class tier that sits above the Opus class in capability. Claude Fable 5, described by Anthropic as its most capable widely released model with state-of-the-art results on nearly all tested benchmarks, is the generally available Mythos-class model: it runs with always-on adaptive thinking, a 1-million-token context window, and 128K output tokens, and includes safety classifiers that automatically fall back to Claude Opus 4.8 for flagged requests in domains such as cybersecurity and biology. Claude Mythos 5 shares the same capabilities without the safety classifiers and is offered only in limited availability through Project Glasswing.
On June 12, 2026, less than a week after this launch, Anthropic announced that it had received a US government export-control directive requiring it to suspend access to both Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5; Anthropic states that complying with the order forces it to disable the two Mythos-class models for all customers, while access to all other Claude models (Opus, Sonnet, and Haiku) remains unaffected and it works to restore access. On June 30, 2026, after the export-control directive was lifted, Anthropic announced that it was redeploying Claude Fable 5 globally (starting July 1, 2026) with updated cybersecurity safeguards, while restoring Claude Mythos 5 access for a set of US organizations. The same day, Anthropic also released Claude Sonnet 5, its most capable Sonnet-tier model, bringing near-Opus intelligence to coding and agentic work at Sonnet cost.
On July 24, 2026, Anthropic released Claude Opus 5, a step-change improvement over Claude Opus 4.8 at the Opus tier, described as coming close to Claude Fable 5's frontier intelligence at half the price: it supports a 1-million-token context window (both the default and the maximum) with 128K output tokens, runs with thinking on by default, and became the new default model on the Claude Max plan.
On September 1, 2026, the Mythos-class tier gained a second generation with Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Mythos 5.1, which keep the same specifications and input and output prices as their predecessors. Three weeks later, on September 22, 2026, Anthropic released Claude Opus 5.5, the first model in the Claude 5.5 family. Anthropic says it performs at the level of Claude Fable 5.1 on most work and costs about 40% less than Claude Opus 5 to run on typical workloads at default settings, and it is the first Opus model to launch with safeguards similar to Claude Fable 5.1's for cybersecurity, biology, and distillation.
The scope of this article is limited to publicly announced models and capabilities documented at
anthropic.com/news/ and the official Claude API documentation. I do not include speculative future models. Pricing details change frequently and are deliberately omitted in favor of links to Anthropic's official pricing page. Benchmark names appear in some of the announcements quoted here; who built the major yardsticks, who declared one saturated, and what replaced it are covered in LLM Benchmark History and Timeline - Who Built Each Yardstick, Who Declared It Saturated, and What Replaced It.
This timeline primarily references the following sources.
- Anthropic News
- Claude API Documentation
- Model deprecations - Claude API
- What's New with AWS - Amazon Bedrock
Claude Model Family Tree (Fable / Opus / Sonnet / Haiku)
Since the Claude 3 generation introduced in March 2024, the family has been organized into three named size tiers: Opus (maximum capability), Sonnet (balanced), and Haiku (low latency, low cost).
The pre-3 generation (Claude 1, Claude Instant, Claude 2, Claude 2.1) predates this naming scheme; in retrospect, Claude 1 and Claude 2 sit on the Opus lineage and Claude Instant sits on the Haiku lineage.
The diagram below shows the full family tree from Claude 1 in 2023 through Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Opus 5.5 in September 2026, including the Mythos-class tier introduced with Claude Fable 5 in June 2026.
The Opus lane covers the largest, most capable models: Claude 1 (March 2023), Claude 2 (July 2023), Claude 2.1 (November 2023), Claude 3 Opus (March 2024), Claude Opus 4 (May 2025), Claude Opus 4.1 (August 2025), Claude Opus 4.5 (November 2025), Claude Opus 4.6 (February 2026), Claude Opus 4.7 (April 2026), Claude Opus 4.8 (May 2026), Claude Opus 5 (July 2026), and Claude Opus 5.5 (September 2026).
The Sonnet lane covers the balanced tier introduced with Claude 3: Claude 3 Sonnet (March 2024), Claude 3.5 Sonnet (June 2024), Claude 3.5 Sonnet new / v2 (October 2024), Claude 3.7 Sonnet (February 2025), Claude Sonnet 4 (May 2025), Claude Sonnet 4.5 (September 2025), Claude Sonnet 4.6 (February 2026), and Claude Sonnet 5 (June 2026).
The Haiku lane is the fastest and lowest-cost tier: Claude Instant (March 2023, retrospectively on the Haiku lineage), Claude 3 Haiku (March 2024), Claude 3.5 Haiku (October 2024 announce, November 2024 availability), and Claude Haiku 4.5 (October 2025). Note that Anthropic has not released Haiku versions corresponding to every Sonnet/Opus minor revision - Haiku 4.0, Haiku 4.6, Haiku 4.7, and Haiku 4.8 do not exist as of September 2026.
In June 2026, the family gained a fourth, Mythos-class tier positioned above the Opus lane: Claude Fable 5 (June 2026) is the generally available Mythos-class model, and Claude Mythos 5 (June 2026) shares the same capabilities without the safety classifiers and is offered in limited availability through Project Glasswing. The tier gained a second generation on September 1, 2026 with Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Mythos 5.1, which keep the same specifications and per-token price and cut cache reads to a quarter of Claude Fable 5's rate.
Timeline of Major Releases
Here is the full chronological timeline of Anthropic Claude model releases and major capability announcements. Each row links to the officialanthropic.com/news/ post or the equivalent official source.
* The table can be sorted by clicking on the column names.
| Date | Event | 
|---|---|
| 2021-01 | Anthropic is founded as an AI safety company by Dario Amodei, Daniela Amodei, and other former OpenAI researchers. | 
| 2022-12-15 | Anthropic publishes the Constitutional AI paper introducing the alignment method that underpins every later Claude model. Source: Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI Feedback. | 
| 2023-03-14 | Claude 1 and Claude Instant are announced and the Anthropic API opens for early access. Source: Introducing Claude. | 
| 2023-05-11 | The context window is expanded from 9K to 100K tokens on Claude. This was the first 100K-token context window from a frontier AI lab. Source: Introducing 100K Context Windows. | 
| 2023-07-11 | Claude 2 is announced with improved coding, math, and reasoning, the public claude.ai chat interface, and a 100K context window. Source: Claude 2. | 
| 2023-08-01 | Claude 2 becomes available on Amazon Bedrock (in preview) with up to 100,000-token context windows, joining Anthropic Claude as a Bedrock preview model ahead of Bedrock's GA. Source: Anthropic's Claude 2 foundation model is now available in Amazon Bedrock. | 
| 2023-09-25 | Anthropic and Amazon announce a strategic collaboration under which Anthropic will make future Claude models available on Amazon Bedrock and use AWS Trainium and Inferentia for training. Source: Anthropic + Amazon. | 
| 2023-09-28 | Amazon Bedrock reaches general availability in US East (N. Virginia) and US West (Oregon) with Anthropic Claude 2 as one of the launch foundation models, alongside models from AI21 Labs, Cohere, Stability AI, and Amazon Titan (with Meta's Llama 2 following soon after). Source: Amazon Bedrock is now generally available. | 
| 2023-11-21 | Claude 2.1 is announced with a 200K-token context window, system prompts, and tool use as a beta. Source: Claude 2.1. | 
| 2024-03-04 | The Claude 3 family is announced (Opus, Sonnet, Haiku), introducing the three-tier naming scheme that all later Claude models follow. Claude 3 is the first Claude family with multimodal (vision) input across every model tier. Claude 3 Opus and Claude 3 Sonnet are available the same day; Claude 3 Haiku follows shortly after. Source: Introducing the next generation of Claude. | 
| 2024-03-13 | Claude 3 Haiku is generally available on the Anthropic API. Source: Claude 3 Haiku - our fastest model yet. | 
| 2024-04-04 | Tool use enters public beta on the Claude API, allowing models to call developer-defined functions. | 
| 2024-05-30 | Tool use becomes generally available on Claude 3 Opus, Sonnet, and Haiku. Source: Tool use is now generally available. | 
| 2024-06-20 | Claude 3.5 Sonnet is announced with significant gains in coding, reasoning, and vision, and at the same price and speed as Claude 3 Sonnet. The same announcement introduces the Artifacts feature in claude.ai . Source: Claude 3.5 Sonnet. | 
| 2024-08-14 | Prompt caching enters public beta on the Anthropic API, allowing developers to cache long repeated prompt prefixes for cost and latency reductions. Source: Prompt caching with Claude. | 
| 2024-10-08 | The Message Batches API enters public beta, enabling asynchronous batch processing of up to 10,000 messages at 50% off standard pricing. Source: Introducing the Message Batches API. | 
| 2024-10-22 | Claude 3.5 Sonnet (new) and Claude 3.5 Haiku are announced, and Computer Use is released as a public beta capability, allowing Claude to perceive and interact with computer interfaces by viewing screens, moving the cursor, clicking, and typing. Source: Introducing computer use, a new Claude 3.5 Sonnet, and Claude 3.5 Haiku. | 
| 2024-11-04 | Claude 3.5 Haiku becomes available on the Anthropic API. | 
| 2025-02-24 | Claude 3.7 Sonnet is announced as Anthropic's first hybrid reasoning model with both standard and extended-thinking modes that the user controls via the API, alongside a research preview of the Claude Code command-line coding agent. Source: Claude 3.7 Sonnet and Claude Code. | 
| 2025-05-22 | Claude Opus 4 and Claude Sonnet 4 are announced, kicking off the Claude 4 generation. Claude Opus 4 is positioned as the world's best coding model at the time of announcement, with extended-thinking with tool use and improved memory features. Claude Code reaches general availability. Source: Introducing Claude 4. | 
| 2025-08-05 | Claude Opus 4.1 is announced with improved coding (74.5% on SWE-bench Verified), research, and data-analysis performance, available on the Claude API, Amazon Bedrock, and Google Cloud Vertex AI. Model identifier claude-opus-4-1-20250805 . Source: Claude Opus 4.1. | 
| 2025-09-29 | Claude Sonnet 4.5 is announced with major coding, instruction-following, and agentic improvements at the same price as Sonnet 4. The same announcement adds a context editing feature and a memory tool to the Claude API. Model identifier claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929 . Source: Claude Sonnet 4.5. | 
| 2025-10-15 | Claude Haiku 4.5 is announced, the first Haiku model to support both extended thinking and Computer Use. It matches Claude Sonnet 4's coding performance at roughly one-third the cost and over twice the speed. Model identifier claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 . Source: Claude Haiku 4.5. | 
| 2025-11-24 | Claude Opus 4.5 is announced with the new effort parameter for balancing capability against cost, context compaction, and a deeper memory tool. Available on the Claude API, Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud Vertex AI, and Microsoft Foundry. Model identifierclaude-opus-4-5-20251101 . Source: Claude Opus 4.5. | 
| 2026-02-05 | Claude Opus 4.6 is announced, inheriting the 1-million-token beta context window (first introduced on Claude Sonnet 4 on 2025-08-12) at the Opus tier, with 128K output tokens, adaptive thinking, and a new Claude Code "agent teams" feature for parallel autonomous work. Model identifier claude-opus-4-6 (first generation to use the dateless pinned-snapshot ID format). Source: Claude Opus 4.6. | 
| 2026-02-17 | Claude Sonnet 4.6 is announced, retaining the 1-million-token beta context window (introduced with Claude Sonnet 4 in August 2025) and adding major improvements in coding and Computer Use. Users preferred Sonnet 4.6 to Opus 4.5 59% of the time. Model identifier claude-sonnet-4-6 . Source: Claude Sonnet 4.6. | 
| 2026-04-16 | Claude Opus 4.7 is announced as the frontier model at the time, with substantial gains on the hardest coding tasks, higher-resolution vision input, a new xhigh effort level, file-system-based memory recall across sessions, and the Task Budgets public beta. Available on the Claude API, Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud Vertex AI, and Microsoft Foundry. Model identifierclaude-opus-4-7 . Source: Claude Opus 4.7. | 
| 2026-05-28 | Claude Opus 4.8 is announced as the new frontier model, roughly 42 days after Opus 4.7 - the shortest gap so far between consecutive Claude Opus releases (versus about 70-75 days for the previous Opus steps). The emphasis is on honesty and reliability (Anthropic reports it is approximately four times less likely than Opus 4.7 to let flaws in code it has written pass unremarked), more efficient tool calling, and better agentic judgment - including stronger computer-use and browser-agent performance (84% on the Online-Mind2Web benchmark, surpassing Opus 4.7) - alongside gains across coding, reasoning, and knowledge work. It launches together with Dynamic Workflows in Claude Code (research preview) - an orchestrator that runs hundreds of parallel subagents that each plan, execute, and verify part of a task - and user-facing effort control for claude.ai and Cowork, plus a fast mode priced about 3x lower than on previous models. Available on the Claude API, Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Foundry. Model identifierclaude-opus-4-8 . Source: Claude Opus 4.8, Claude Opus 4.8 is now available on AWS. |
